title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This page is the single-source handbook reference for new and current Redwood employees. It summarizes what it means to work at Redwood, role and career ladder expectations, our benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding process, and the primary internal tools you will use day-to-day. Use the links in the Related pages section for deep dives (hiring templates, HR policies, engineering career ladders). This document is maintained by People Ops; please send feedback or corrections to people-ops@redwood.ai.

1. Working at Redwood — culture & principles

Short intro: Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on building a production-grade LLM inference platform. Our culture emphasizes ownership, continuous improvement, engineering craftsmanship, and customer-focus. We value:

- Shipping: prioritize customer impact and measurable outcomes.
- Reliability and clarity: document decisions, write clear runbooks, and own the SLOs your product depends on.
- Experimentation with guardrails: run small experiments, measure, and rollback when necessary.
- Respect and inclusion: we hire diverse perspectives and create psychological safety for difficult conversations.

Working norms (high level):

- Core hours: asynchronous first, with core overlap from 11:00–16:00 PT for cross-team meetings.
- Meeting etiquette: add clear agenda and decision notes; default to 30 minutes unless pre-approved.
- Communication: use Slack for operational coordination, Confluence for long-lived docs, and Loom for walkthroughs.

2. Roles & Career ladders

Purpose: give a clear, consistent expectation framework for individual contributors (IC), managers, and cross-functional roles. All career ladders follow the same principles: scope, impact, technical/functional depth, collaboration, and leadership.

High-level ladder (engineering example):

- IC1 (Associate Engineer): Focused on learning the codebase and delivering small features or bug fixes with guidance.
- IC2 (Engineer): Owns small components, shipping features independently, writing reliable tests and docs.
- IC3 (Senior Engineer): Drives design for larger components, mentors peers, and contributes to cross-team initiatives.
- IC4 (Staff Engineer): Technical leader across teams, shapes architecture, leads large projects, and drives technical strategy.
- IC5 (Principal Engineer): Company-wide technical leadership, sets long-term direction, represents Redwood externally for technical topics.
- IC6 (Distinguished/Architect): Exceptional technical career path for breakthrough technical contributions.

Manager ladder (brief):

- M1 (Engineering Manager): Manages a small team, owns delivery and career growth.
- M2 (Senior Eng Manager): Leads multiple teams or a larger function, sets operational goals.
- M3+ (Director / VP): Strategic leadership, cross-org priorities, and org design.

Promotion and calibration process (summary):

1. Candidate prepares a promotion packet: accomplishments, examples mapped to rubric, peer feedback.
2. Manager provides written assessment and compiles evidence.
3. Calibration: People Ops and cross-functional leaders review packets quarterly.
4. Decision communicated with growth plan and updated expectations.

Promotion timeline expectations: most promotions follow a minimum tenure in role (typically 12–24 months) and require clear evidence of increased scope and impact. Exceptions are rare and documented in the promotion packet.

3. Benefits & perks (summary table)

Below is a concise summary; see the full benefits policy for legal and eligibility requirements.

| Category | Core offering | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Health | Medical (PPO/HMO), Dental, Vision | Company covers 80% of employee premium; dependents optional |
| Paid Time Off | 20 days PTO + company holidays | 1st-year accrual prorated; flexible parental leave policy (16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary) |
| Retirement | 401(k) with 4% match | Immediate vesting of match after 1 year |
| Equity | RSUs for full-time employees | Standard 4-year vesting, 1-year cliff |
| Compensation | Market-competitive salary + performance bonus | Annual calibration and banding review |
| Learning & Development | $1,500 L&D stipend / year | Course and conference reimbursement process in People Ops portal |
| Remote/home setup | $1,000 one-time remote stipend; ergonomic equipment budget | Submit receipts to payroll within 60 days |

Perks and wellbeing:

- Monthly wellness stipend and mental health coverage (therapy EAP).
- Commuter stipend for local employees.
- Quarterly company offsites and team budgets for social events.
- Employee referral bonuses and recognition programs.

How to access benefits: log into the People Ops portal (HRIS link provided in the onboarding checklist). For questions, contact benefits@redwood.ai.

4. Hiring & interviewing overview

Goal: hire high-quality, mission-aligned talent while providing a consistent, respectful candidate experience.

Hiring workflow (steps):

1. Requisition & role spec: Hiring manager creates a req in Greenhouse with a clear role description and success criteria.
2. Sourcing & screening: Recruiter screens and sends first-pass phone screen. Use the standard scorecard (linked in Related pages).
3. On-site loop: typically 4–5 interviews covering technical depth, system design, collaboration, and role-specific skills. Include a take-home or live exercise only when necessary.
4. Calibration & offer: Hiring manager compiles interview feedback, recruiter prepares compensation and levels. Compensation and role approvals go through People Ops and Finance.
5. Offer & acceptance: Recruiter extends offer; candidate sign-offs include equity, benefits, start date, and paperwork.

Interviewer guidelines (short):

- Use the standard rubric and leave detailed feedback within 48 hours.
- Avoid illegal or inappropriate questions (see EEO policy).
- Prioritize candidate experience: timely communication and clear timelines.

Diversity & Inclusion: Redwood runs structured interview training and diverse slate goals for officer-level hiring. Please coordinate with Talent Acquisition for difficult-to-fill roles.

5. Onboarding — 30/60/90 plan and checklist

Onboarding objective: accelerate new hires to full productivity while ensuring they feel welcomed and supported. The People Ops and hiring manager co-own onboarding.

Pre-boarding tasks (before day 1):

- Recruiter sends welcome packet, benefits links, start date, and laptop shipping details.
- People Ops creates HRIS profile, payroll setup, and schedules new hire orientation.
- Eng manager raises access request in IT ticketing system (GitHub, AWS, Slack, internal Confluence access).

Day 1–7 (orientation & setup):

1. Day 1: Welcome meeting with People Ops, orientation overview, benefits enrollment walkthrough.
2. Tech setup: ensure hardware arrived, MFA configured, and access to GitHub, CI/CD, Slack, and the internal dev environment.
3. Buddy assignment: a peer buddy is assigned for social onboarding and immediate questions.

30/60/90 expectations (manager-provided):

- 30 days: complete required trainings, merge first small PR, and present a short "first-week" summary in team meeting.
- 60 days: own a medium-sized feature or bug fix, complete at least one on-call shadowing session (if applicable).
- 90 days: independently deliver a cross-functional project and have initial 90-day review with manager and People Ops.

Checklist: required trainings (security, data handling, SSO & MFA), optional trainings (system design bootcamp, infra deep-dive). All required trainings must be completed within the first 30 days.

6. Internal tools guide (quick reference)

Primary platforms — what to know: 

- Slack: primary operational chat; teams use #team-* channels. Use status and Do Not Disturb for heads-down time. Slack apps: PagerDuty integration, Standup bot.
- Confluence: canonical docs and runbooks. Create pages using the company template; add reviewer and owner metadata to long-lived docs.
- GitHub: monorepo for service code and infra. Branch naming: feature/<team>-<short-desc>. Use PR template and required checks.
- CI/CD (CircleCI): pipelines are defined in .circleci/config.yml. Tagging and release: follow the Release Playbook (linked).
- Issue tracking (Jira): use the Team board; follow the label taxonomy: epic/component/priority.
- Cloud console / IAM (AWS): access via SSO; requests go through IT tickets. For Dedicated/Private customer environments, request separate cross-account roles.
- Observability: Grafana (dashboards), Tempo/Jaeger (traces), Loki/Datadog (logs). For on-call runbooks, see the eng-sre runbooks page.

Common commands / examples (engineering):

- Clone monorepo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra.git
- Start local dev: yarn start:dev (see README in /eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates)
- Create a release PR: ./scripts/release.sh --minor

Security & access notes: request all production access through the IT ticketing portal. MFA is required for cloud console and GitHub admin access. Never store secrets in plain text; use Vault or the Secrets Manager integration.

7. Performance & feedback cycle

Performance reviews: semi-annual review cadence with mid-year check-ins. Managers collect peer feedback and map feedback to the role rubric.

1:1s and career development: managers should hold weekly 1:1s and document outcomes in the People Ops template. Career conversations are encouraged year-round.

8. Useful contacts and owners

- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai (benefits, L&D, policies)
- IT / Access requests: it-ops@redwood.ai (hardware, SSO, production access)
- Security: security@redwood.ai (incidents, threat reporting, vulnerability disclosure)
- Payroll & finance questions: payroll@redwood.ai
- Hiring & Talent Acquisition: recruiting@redwood.ai

9. Governance, updates, and doc ownership

This handbook is owned by People Ops. Updates are published quarterly or as policy changes dictate. When proposing changes:

1. Create a draft Confluence page and add People Ops as reviewer.
2. Add a changelog entry at the top of the page with date and author.

3. Notify People Ops and the employee distribution list for substantial policy changes.

Appendix A — quick reference table

- New hire first week: orientation, benefits enrollment, tech access, buddy assigned.
- Promotion packet owners: candidate + manager + People Ops.
- Required trainings: Security, Data Handling, SSO & MFA.
